verdict.headline: September hiring falls far short of forecasts with long-term yields just under their 2002 high
verdict.label: Payrolls +29,000 vs ~90,000 expected; unemployment 4.2%; Aug revised to 133,000. Before the release: S&P 500 futures +0.4%, Nasdaq-100 futures +0.6%; 30Y ~5.618% (2002 high 5.644%), 10Y ~5.243%, 2Y ~4.79%; Oct hike odds ~35%; Brent ~$102; gold ~$4,179; BTC ~$86,460.
verdict.rationale_short: The economy added 29,000 jobs in September against about 90,000 expected, below the lowest of 27 forecasts FactSet collected; unemployment rose to 4.2% and August was revised down to 133,000. The print lands with the thirty-year yield at about 5.618%, 2.6 basis points under its 2002 high. On Thursday the two-year fell 9 basis points as October hike odds dropped to about 35%, while long yields barely moved, which suggested the pressure on long bonds is not mainly about the Fed; oil near $102 and government-bond selling abroad are still in place. Whether the thirty-year follows the two-year lower on a print this weak is the test of that read. A thirty-year close above 5.644% would resume the rise; a close under 5.44% would say it is fading.
verdict.lede_short: US employers added just 29,000 jobs in September, against about 90,000 expected, and unemployment rose to 4.2%. The print should cut October rate-hike odds further, but on Thursday long-term yields barely moved as short-term ones fell, so the test is whether the 30-year, near 5.62%, follows. A 30-year close above its 2002 high of 5.644% would resume the rise; one under 5.44% would say it is fading.

supporting_data.label: Payrolls rose 29,000 in September against about 90,000 expected, unemployment rose to 4.2% and August was revised down to 133,000 — the print missed even the lowest FactSet forecast of 60,000, and should cut October hike odds further.
The thirty-year rose about 1 basis point to 5.618% and the ten-year held near 5.243% before payrolls — long yields are holding Thursday's levels rather than extending the pullback.

The two-year fell 9 basis points on Thursday to just under 4.80% while the ten-year closed about 4 basis points lower — the curve steepened, so falling hike odds are reaching short yields but not long ones.
October hike odds stood near 35% on CME FedWatch at Thursday's close, from about 71% a week earlier — a 29,000 payroll print argues for that decline continuing.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 2.6% to 23,972.29, its lowest since July, on its first session back from holiday — it priced a week of higher global yields in one day while US futures rose.
Nike fell 9.6% pre-market to about $31.79 after guiding fiscal 2027 revenue down by a high single-digit percentage — with September hiring at 29,000, demand outside AI is weakening on two fronts.

watchlist_mentions.note: Third-quarter deliveries due today against a company-compiled consensus of 461,974, down 7.1% from a year earlier; estimates range from about 422,000 to 482,000.
Up about 3% over 24 hours to about $86,460 ahead of payrolls, rising with stock futures while the dollar sits near its 2026 high.

trade_setups.thesis: Payrolls rose only 29,000 with the thirty-year 2.6 basis points under its 2002 high; whether it follows the two-year lower tests how much of the long-end rise is about the Fed.
trade_setups.entry: Thirty-year ~5.618% between the 2002 high of 5.644% above and 5.44% below.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close above 5.644% on a print this weak would say the pressure is not about the Fed; a close under 5.44% would say the rise is fading.
trade_setups.horizon: Today's payrolls through next Wednesday's Fed minutes

trade_setups.thesis: Nike's guide and General Mills at a 52-week low point to weaker spending outside AI; Tesla deliveries are today's next read.
trade_setups.entry: Tesla consensus 461,974 deliveries, range about 422,000 to 482,000; Nike ~$31.79 pre-market.
trade_setups.invalidation: Deliveries above consensus alongside firm payrolls would weaken the read.

trade_setups.thesis: Hong Kong fell 2.6% to a July low as US futures rose; the US market has stood apart from the global response to higher yields.
trade_setups.invalidation: An S&P 500 close under 7,600 with the thirty-year above 5.644% would mean US stocks are following the rest of the world; a close above 7,666.45 with yields under the line would keep the gap open.
